discovery: Discovery that living cells organise their interior through liquid-liquid phase separation into biomolecular condensates

nominees.name: Anthony A. Hyman
nominees.affiliation: Max Planck Institute of Molecular Cell Biology and Genetics, Dresden, Germany

nominees.name: Frank Jülicher
nominees.affiliation: Max Planck Institute for the Physics of Complex Systems, Dresden, Germany

motivation: In 2009 Brangwynne, Hyman and Jülicher showed that P granules in C. elegans embryos are liquid droplets that form by phase separation and dissolve again, governed by the same thermodynamics as condensation in simple fluids. This changed how we understand cellular organisation: membraneless compartments such as nucleoli, stress granules and signalling clusters are now understood as condensates whose formation, size and dynamics follow from phase diagrams, surface tension, coarsening and active, non-equilibrium control. Jülicher supplied the theoretical framework, including the theory of droplet positioning and size control by chemical activity. The idea has opened a large research field linking statistical physics with molecular biology, with consequences for neurodegenerative disease, where aberrant liquid-to-solid transitions lead to aggregation. It is a clear case of basic physical concepts explaining a central problem in living matter, and it has been confirmed many times by quantitative experiment and simulation.
